analysis.analysis: The overall churn rate is 9.0%, indicating that 9 out of every 100 customers are leaving, while the retention rate is 91.0%, suggesting that the majority of customers are staying. However, the number of retained customers is 1890, which shows a significant base of loyal customers. The churn rates vary by channel, with Facebook showing the highest churn rate at 13.0%, while Email has the lowest at 6.0%. This indicates potential issues with customer satisfaction or engagement in certain channels. The total revenue at risk due to churn is substantial, as the business generated a total revenue of 12950.0, meaning that losing customers could significantly impact future earnings. The number of new customers is 483, which could indicate a leaky bucket scenario if retention does not improve. Overall, while retention is relatively high, the varying churn rates across channels suggest that some channels may be underperforming in retaining customers.
detected_issues: High churn rate in Facebook channel at 13.0%
Low retention in Google Ads channel at 89.0%
analysis.root_cause_hypothesis: The primary root cause appears to be related to customer engagement and satisfaction issues in specific channels, particularly Facebook and Google Ads.
business_risks: Potential revenue loss due to high churn rates in certain channels.
Risk of customer dissatisfaction leading to further churn if not addressed.

recommendations.title: Reduce spend on Facebook acquisition
recommendations.whats_happening: Facebook has the highest customer churn at 13 percent, above the overall 9 percent churn.
evidence: Facebook churn rate is 13 percent compared to overall churn of 9 percent

what_you_should_do.step: Decrease Facebook advertising budget by 30 percent
what_you_should_do.how: Open budget settings for Spring Launch campaign, reduce daily budget to 70 percent of current amount, and save changes
guardrails: Do not reduce total conversions below 150 per week
Monitor reach and impression frequency to avoid under delivery

what_you_should_do.step: Allocate freed budget to email retention efforts
what_you_should_do.how: Increase budget or resource allocation for email retention automation by the equivalent spend amount
guardrails: Keep total email sends under current daily limits

recommendations.why_this_matters: Shifting away from the highest churn source and focusing on stable channels should lower overall churn and boost retention.

expected_impact.explanation: By reducing new customers from the highest churn source and reallocating to reliable channels, overall churn rate will drop.

dependency_or_risk: Requires email system capacity to handle additional sends
Risk of reduced new customer volume if not offset by other channels

measurement_plan.how_to_measure: Compare overall churn rate two weeks before and two weeks after budget reallocation
measurement_plan.success_criteria: Churn rate decreases from 9 percent to at least 8 percent
measurement_plan.notes: Allow one-week lag for ad budget changes to stabilize

recommendations.title: Launch re-engagement email sequence for at-risk customers
recommendations.whats_happening: Customers at risk of churn are not being actively re-engaged. Email channel has the best retention rate at 94 percent.
evidence: Email channel retention rate is 94 percent, with churn at only 6 percent

what_you_should_do.step: Identify customers with no purchase in the last 30 days
what_you_should_do.how: Create a segment filter for customers whose last purchase date is 30 days or more ago
guardrails: Segment size between 10,000 and 20,000 customers to ensure deliverability

what_you_should_do.step: Design a four-part email series with personalized content and special offers
what_you_should_do.how: Include product recommendations based on purchase history and a 10 percent discount code
guardrails: Limit discount to one per customer
Use simple subject lines

what_you_should_do.step: Schedule the drip to send one email every 5 days
what_you_should_do.how: Set an interval of five days between each email for the at-risk segment
guardrails: Ensure no more than one email is sent per week to any customer

recommendations.why_this_matters: Targeted reminders and offers via email encourage repeat purchases and reduce churn.

expected_impact.explanation: Regular engagement and exclusive offers will prompt repeat buying, raising retention rate.

dependency_or_risk: Potential increase in unsubscribes if content is not relevant

measurement_plan.how_to_measure: Compare retention rate of the targeted segment before and four weeks after the email sequence
measurement_plan.success_criteria: Retention rate of the targeted segment increases by at least 2 percent
measurement_plan.notes: Monitor unsubscribe rates and segment engagement

recommendations.title: Add remarketing lists in Google Ads for repeat purchase
recommendations.whats_happening: Google Ads channel has an 11 percent churn rate, below the best channels, indicating customers could be re-engaged with targeted ads.
evidence: Google Ads churn rate is 11 percent versus email channel churn at 6 percent

what_you_should_do.step: Build a customer match list of past buyers
what_you_should_do.how: Upload a hashed list of customer emails from the past year per platform guidelines
guardrails: Ensure list has at least 1,000 active customer records

what_you_should_do.step: Apply the list to search campaigns with bid adjustment
what_you_should_do.how: Attach the customer match audience to active ad groups and set a bid increase of 20 percent
guardrails: Do not exceed maximum bid by more than 50 percent

recommendations.why_this_matters: Remarketing to past customers on search prompts repeat orders and helps lower churn.

expected_impact.explanation: Targeted ads remind past customers of the brand when they search, driving repeat purchases and reducing churn.

dependency_or_risk: Requires compliance with data privacy rules
Initial list size may be small

measurement_plan.how_to_measure: Compare churn rate of customers in the remarketing list to a control group over two weeks
measurement_plan.success_criteria: Churn rate of remarketed customers falls below 9 percent

recommendations.title: Update landing page to reduce bounce and drive retention
recommendations.whats_happening: Email-driven sessions have the highest bounce rate at 36 percent, losing engagement before retention offers.
evidence: Bounce rate on email channel landing page is 36 percent compared to the 30 percent overall average

what_you_should_do.step: Create a landing page variant highlighting loyalty benefits above the fold
what_you_should_do.how: Add a section detailing loyalty points and rewards with a clear call to action button
guardrails: Keep page load time under 3 seconds
Maintain existing main navigation

what_you_should_do.step: Run an A/B test with 50 percent of email traffic
what_you_should_do.how: Split email visitors evenly between current page and new variant
guardrails: End test after at least 1,000 sessions per variant

what_you_should_do.step: Analyze results and implement the winner
what_you_should_do.how: Compare bounce rate and engagement metrics between variants
guardrails: Require at least a 5 percent improvement in bounce rate

recommendations.why_this_matters: Reducing bounce keeps visitors engaged, increasing the chance of repeat purchase and raising retention.

expected_impact.explanation: Improved engagement on landing page drives more repeat purchases, boosting retention rate.

dependency_or_risk: External traffic changes may skew results

measurement_plan.how_to_measure: Compare bounce rate and retention for email traffic before and after the A/B test
measurement_plan.success_criteria: Bounce rate drops by at least 5 percent and retention increases by 1 percent
measurement_plan.notes: Seasonal trends may affect web traffic patterns

recommendations.title: Launch SMS loyalty program invitation
recommendations.whats_happening: SMS has a strong conversion rate but still sees 9 percent churn. It can drive deeper loyalty.
evidence: SMS channel conversion rate is 19.6 percent with a churn rate of 9 percent

what_you_should_do.step: Design an SMS message offering loyalty program enrollment
what_you_should_do.how: Use a template with a short link to the loyalty signup page
guardrails: Limit to one message per week
Comply with opt-in regulations

what_you_should_do.step: Send SMS to customers with two or more purchases in last year
what_you_should_do.how: Filter by purchase history and send campaign
guardrails: Exclude customers already enrolled in the loyalty program

what_you_should_do.step: Send a reminder SMS one week later to non-responders
what_you_should_do.how: Set a one-week delay and filter for non-enrollees
guardrails: Cap total messages at two per customer

recommendations.why_this_matters: Encouraging loyalty program sign-ups gives customers incentive to repeat purchases, reducing churn.

expected_impact.explanation: Loyalty rewards prompt repeat orders, increasing total retained customers.

dependency_or_risk: Signup landing page must convert well

measurement_plan.how_to_measure: Compare loyalty sign-ups and retention change among SMS recipients to previous period
measurement_plan.success_criteria: At least 10 percent of messaged customers sign up and their retention rises by 5 percent
measurement_plan.notes: Monitor for message fatigue and opt-out rates

recommendations.title: Implement cohort-based churn tracking
recommendations.whats_happening: Current reporting shows overall churn but lacks detail on when and why customers leave.
evidence: Analysis shows churn rate only at campaign level, no cohort breakdown

what_you_should_do.step: Set up cohorts by acquisition month in analytics platform
what_you_should_do.how: Create cohort reports grouping users by first purchase date
guardrails: Limit cohorts to the last six months for performance

what_you_should_do.step: Build a dashboard showing retention and churn per cohort
what_you_should_do.how: Use cohort report data to visualize month-over-month retention curves
guardrails: Refresh data daily
Limit display to six cohort lines at once

what_you_should_do.step: Train teams on interpreting cohort reports
what_you_should_do.how: Host a one-hour workshop with marketing and analytics teams
guardrails: Keep session under 60 minutes

recommendations.why_this_matters: Cohort tracking reveals when churn spikes occur, guiding targeted retention actions.

expected_impact.explanation: Better visibility allows timely actions to prevent churn and maintain retention.

dependency_or_risk: Data integration complexity may delay setup

measurement_plan.how_to_measure: Validate cohort retention metrics against historical data
measurement_plan.success_criteria: Cohort retention metrics are accurate and updated daily
measurement_plan.notes: Initial reports may have incomplete data due to integration lag

recommendations.title: Update Facebook ad creative to focus on community and testimonials
recommendations.whats_happening: Current Facebook ads may not engage existing customers, contributing to 13 percent churn.
evidence: Facebook churn rate is highest at 13 percent and click rate is 4 percent, below email and SMS

what_you_should_do.step: Develop three new ad creative variants featuring customer success stories
what_you_should_do.how: Collect testimonials, overlay on image, and include a clear call to action to join loyalty program
guardrails: Use existing brand guidelines
Keep text under 20 percent of image

what_you_should_do.step: Run a controlled test splitting audience between old and new creative
what_you_should_do.how: Set up an A/B test with 50 percent of audience for each creative set
guardrails: Limit test budget to 20 percent of total Facebook spend

what_you_should_do.step: Review engagement and churn metrics after two weeks
what_you_should_do.how: Compare comment and share rates and retention changes for each audience group
guardrails: Require statistical significance at 90 percent

recommendations.why_this_matters: Ads that resonate with customers can boost engagement and reduce churn on Facebook.

expected_impact.explanation: Higher engagement from community-focused ads keeps customers connected, lowering churn.

dependency_or_risk: Creative production time may delay test
Test sample size may be small initially

measurement_plan.how_to_measure: Compare churn and engagement rates for audiences exposed to new versus old creative
measurement_plan.success_criteria: Churn for new creative group falls below 13 percent and engagement increases by 10 percent
measurement_plan.notes: Extend test if sample size is small
